clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; his wife Celeste separated from him in August; your mother lay awake over them both; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. By May 1979, your grandmother took a job at the library and was out of the house each day, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother being ordered to bed for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984, within four months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and by September when your sister Ines was born, the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis with Parkinson's disease in September 1986, over the next ten years: your grandfather Ambrose overfunctioned, taking over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her; the two brothers argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather's chest pains began; your grandmother's functioning declined through falls and loss of mobility; your father overfunctioned taking her to the clinic; his sister Mavis came to stay one week in four to nurse her; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl's anxiety rose with panic spells; and your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side. By June 1997, your grandmother moved to the nursing home, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job at the mines up north in May 1999, within about a year: your father and brother argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, even to work; and by August 2000, Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the year: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and lost the job in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; and by November you took a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again, and the shifts settled. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.
